Updated Module 2.4.Section Header: Overview of the Nonclinical Testing Strategy
Updated Module 2.4.Content: Identify where literature data were used to supplement proprietary studies; full citations are provided in Module 4.
Primary pharmacology summary: dose-response/concentration-response relationships for all key effects across species
Secondary pharmacology: key findings most relevant to human risk (e.g., off-target receptor binding that may be clinically significant)
Summarize core safety pharmacology findings (CNS, cardiovascular, respiratory) and integrate these results with repeat-dose toxicology assessments (e.g., QTc / ICH S7B) where applicable
Safety pharmacology: follow-up/ancillary studies (e.g., renal, GI, autonomic)
Immunogenicity impact on pharmacology (biologics)
Discussion of MOA and relevance to human
Exposure–response (PK/PD) relationships across species
In vitro–in vivo correlation/translatability
Demonstrate binding or target engagement in the species used for testing and in humans, confirming the scientific relevance of chosen models.
Describe relevant pharmacodynamic interactions, particularly if co-administration with other agents is anticipated clinically.
Disease model evaluation (if applicable)
Significance of unexpected or secondary pharmacologic effects
Clinical implications of pharmacodynamic findings
Note any literature or reference-product data supporting pharmacologic characterization; complete citations appear in Module 4.
Summarize absorption data from all administered routes and formulations, noting vehicle or formulation effects and how routes relate to intended clinical use.
Summarize systemic exposure and bioavailability across doses and species, including assessment of dose proportionality (PK linearity or non-linearity) and any food or formulation-related effects.
Distribution: plasma protein binding across species

Summarize tissue distribution studies, including radiolabel or reporter-based (e.g., GFP/luciferase) biodistribution when relevant for modality (e.g., mRNA vaccines). Note when such studies were not required.
Describe any dedicated organ-transfer studies only where clinically relevant (e.g., expected CNS or reproductive exposure).
Outline metabolic pathways and enzymes characterized; for ADCs, focus on the small-molecule payload component.
Include evaluation of metabolite profiles and serum stability, particularly for ADCs or unstable bioconjugates.
Excretion: routes and recovery (urine, feces, bile, expired air)

Describe the bioanalytical methods used to quantify the drug and metabolites, including key validation parameters and any notable deviations from standard practice. Summarize PK modeling approaches applied to interpret exposure data, noting that modeling may be optional depending on the molecule type.
PK linearity or departure from linearity and mechanism
Target saturation or TMDD (for biologics)
Present comparative exposure data (AUC, Cmax) to aid human dose-selection modeling
Assessment of analytical method relevance and PK models used
Evaluation of toxicokinetic data and exposure supporting NOAEL interpretation
Inconsistencies in PK or TK data and interpretation
Species comparison tables/figures summarizing NOAEL and toxic-dose exposures vs human MRHD (AUC, Cmax)
Summarize the impact of anti-drug antibodies (if observed) on systemic exposure and clearance in nonclinical studies.
Species comparison (highlighting most relevant species and rationale)
Address potential PK interactions if mechanistically or clinically plausible (e.g., for ADC small-molecule components).
Other PK studies (special populations or disease models if applicable)
In vitro–in vivo correlation/translatability
Single-dose toxicity: overall summary (LD50 or MTD; if performed)
Repeat-dose toxicity: pivotal NOAELs by species/route/duration
Repeat-dose toxicity: critical target organ findings (nature, severity, reversibility)
Onset, severity, duration, dose-dependency, and reversibility of toxic effects
Species- or sex-related differences in toxicity
Causes of death and pathologic findings summary
Genotoxicity: summary of study results (e.g., gene mutation, chromosomal aberration, in vivo assays) and interpretation in the context of the molecule’s chemical structure and mechanism of action.
Carcinogenicity: rationale and study design (if applicable)
Carcinogenic potential and human risk assessment (structure, genotox, exposure, epidemiology if available)
Reproductive/developmental toxicity: summary of fertility, embryo-fetal, and pre/postnatal findings
Juvenile animal studies (if conducted): justification and key outcomes
Summarize local tolerance findings for the intended route of administration (e.g., injection site or topical irritation)
Other toxicity studies: antigenicity/immunogenicity/hypersensitivity/impurities/metabolites etc. (as applicable)
Immunotoxicity/immune function assessments (including ADA-mediated effects)
Phototoxicity and photosafety (if relevant)
Extrapolation of animal toxicity data to humans (species, routes, duration, exposures, margins)
Safety pharmacology findings integrated with toxicology (e.g., QTc/ICH S7B considerations)
TK/PK overview: demonstration of systemic exposure in all studies
Relationship between toxicity and pharmacology
Integrated pharmacology-PK-toxicology analysis
Adequacy of nonclinical package for proposed clinical use
Overall human risk assessment based on nonclinical data
Key safety concerns and proposed mitigation strategies
Comparison to class effects or related products
Address special population considerations only when nonclinical data indicate altered exposure or risk
Predictivity to clinic — alignment of nonclinical signals with observed/anticipated clinical AEs
Discuss impurity/degradant qualification when levels exceed established qualification thresholds
Material differences vs commercial product (chirality, chemical form, impurity profile) and their impact
Justify the proposed starting clinical dose using NOAEL- or exposure-based approaches (e.g., MABEL), and describe the planned dose escalation strategy.
Dose escalation rationale and maximum tolerated dose projection
Include clinical monitoring elements when directly supported by nonclinical safety signals (e.g., organ-specific toxicity, immune activation).
Labeling implications for pregnancy, lactation, pediatric use
Overall benefit-risk assessment supporting clinical development
Outstanding issues and follow-up studies only if specific regulatory interactions have already defined an agreed risk-resolution path.
Conclusions
Implications for product labeling (precautions/warnings/contraindications)
Complete list of cited references
References formatted per ICH M4 guidelines
Key references provided as full text (if used in lieu of studies)
Citations to Tabulated Summaries in format “(Table X.X, Study/Report Number)”

Updated Module 2.6.Content: Provide a high-level overview of the nonclinical program and proposed clinical use. Tabular summaries may be used, but include brief methodological context (e.g., route, dose ranges, systems assessed) to ensure results are interpretable without raw data.
Identify the drug substance/product using the development code or internal name if no INN is assigned. Include dosage form(s), strength(s), and intended clinical route(s).
Incl. chemical structure diagram (or description for biologics including sequence/format, e.g., mAb isotype).
Provide a brief statement of pharmacologic class and intended MOA, with detailed primary PD evidence cross-referenced to Section 2.6.2.2.
State proposed clinical indication(s) with brief rationale (disease area, unmet need).
State proposed clinical dose range(s), frequency, and duration of use relevant to target population.
State intended patient population (adult/pediatric), special populations (renal/hepatic impairment), and expected concomitant meds.
Point to where detailed data are summarized (2.6.2–2.6.6) and tabulated (2.6.3, 2.6.5, 2.6.7).

Provide a concise overview of the pharmacology package (in vitro and in vivo systems and species used), with clear direction to the detailed subsections that follow. Do not repeat mechanistic narrative from Module 2.4.
Note notable features or gaps (e.g., no relevant disease model available, reliance on surrogate endpoints).
State key findings supporting intended MOA and on-target activity across systems.
ID findings that signal potential off-target or adverse effects (pointer to safety pharm/secondary PD).

Provide a concise narrative summary. Do not repeat data already presented in tables; instead, reference specific tables or study report numbers as needed. If certain mechanistic, histopathology, or literature findings are not captured in subsequent sections, they may be briefly included here to maintain completeness and relevance

Summarize in vitro binding and functional activity data, including assay systems, controls, potency, and selectivity. Include cross-reactivity with homologous targets and cross-species target homology to support relevance of animal models.
Summ. in vivo proof-of-pharmacology models demonstrating efficacy-relevant endpoints and exposure-response.
Disc. species/model relevance to human disease pathophysiology and target homology.
Comp. potency/selectivity vs class comparators; contextualize therapeutic index where known.
Note concentration/occupancy Required for effect; relate to achievable human exposures at proposed doses.
Note whether any tolerance or desensitization has been observed; if not evaluated, avoids suggesting additional work is expected
State that pharmacology studies are typically non-GLP and indicate GLP status only where applicable.

Secondary pharmacology studies are generally not required unless indicated by target biology or unexpected findings in primary PD or toxicology studies. If conducted, summarize any off-target or system-level pharmacology by organ system; if not conducted, state that no secondary pharmacology evaluations were warranted.
ID meaningful off-target activities (e.g., receptor binding <100x selectivity, ion channel modulation) that may predict risk, if relevant
Disc. dose/exposure relationship of off-target findings and translational relevance to human exposure margins, if relevant
Integrate secondary PD findings that predict adverse effects with Safety Pharmacology where applicable
State any negative findings to define the safety profile breadth (e.g., no meaningful hERG inhibition up to X µM).

Summ. dedicated core battery studies (CV: hERG/ion channels, in vivo QT/QTc; CNS: FOB/locomotor; respiratory: plethysmography), typically performed under GLP and often integrated into repeat-dose toxicology studies.
Summ. follow-up/ supplemental organ system studies as warranted (renal, GI motility/secretion, vascular tone).
Present study design basics (species/strain, route, dose levels, positive controls, timing, endpoints).
Note key effects (onset, magnitude, dose-response), reversibility, and safety margins vs expected human exposure.
Indicate GLP compliance and justify any deviations; reference ICH S7A/S7B where relevant.

Summ. PD interaction studies (e.g., additive/synergistic/antagonistic effects with standard-of-care or another investigational agent). These are required if the product is intended for combination use; otherwise, PD interaction studies are not warranted. These interaction studies do not replace the independent evaluation of each agent’s safety and efficacy.
Desc. models, dosing regimens, endpoints, and observed interaction nature and magnitude.
Disc. translational relevance given clinical co-medications and exposure overlap.
Integrate primary, secondary, and safety pharmacology; define overall pharmacology profile and benefit-risk hypotheses.
Acknowledge inconsistencies, uncertainties, and model limitations; best practices to discuss with FDA in pre-IND meeting
Rel. pharmacology margins to human MRHD exposure; identify monitoring strategies for predicted risks.
Incl. tables/figures within text or appended; ensure units/labels are consistent; cross-reference as (Table X.X, Study/Report Number).
Prov. one-line entry per pharmacology report: study type, test system, route, facility, study/report number, CTD location, GLP footnote. Column structure may be adapted based on dataset organization.

Columns: Study Type; Test System; Method/Route; Species/Strain; Dose/Conc; Key Endpoints; Key Results; GLP; Study/Report No.; CTD Location. Column structure may be adapted based on dataset organization.

Columns: Organ System; Test System; Method/Route; Species/Strain; Dose/Conc; Endpoints; Noteworthy Off-target Findings; GLP; Study/Report No.; CTD Location. Column structure may be adapted based on dataset organization.

Columns: Organ System; Species/Strain; Method/Route; Doses (mg/kg); Sex/Group n; Noteworthy Findings; GLP; Study/Report No.; CTD Location. Column structure may be adapted based on dataset organization.
Columns: Interacting Agent; Model; Doses/Regimens; Endpoints; Direction of Interaction; Magnitude; GLP; Study/Report No.; CTD Location. Column structure may be adapted based on dataset organization.
Summ. PK package scope: species/strains, routes, formulations, and alignment with pharm/tox studies.
State key ADME findings and exposure ranges relevant to efficacy and safety.
ID analytical platforms used across studies and comparability considerations.

Summarize bioanalytical methods used across animal and clinical matrices, noting validation status and assay performance (LOD/LOQ, accuracy, precision). Include dose formulation analysis relevant to toxicology studies.
Prov. detection/quantification limits (LOD/LOQ), accuracy/precision, selectivity, carryover assessments.
Disc. stability of analytes in matrix (bench-top, freeze-thaw, long-term) and sample handling effects.
State any method changes across studies and their impact on comparability/interpretation.

Summarize the rate and extent of absorption for each route of administration used, including key PK parameters (e.g., Cmax, Tmax, AUC) and any notable features such as lag time or flip-flop kinetics where observed. Ensure both oral and non-oral routes (e.g., IV, SC, IN) are included where applicable.

Report bioavailability only for non-IV routes (e.g., SC, IN) and discuss factors that may influence absorption (e.g., formulation, dose level). Where available, reference TK data from GLP toxicology studies to support exposure estimates. For IV administration, note that absolute bioavailability is inherently 100% and does not require further discussion.
Incl. in situ/in vitro permeability/transport data if used to explain in vivo absorption differences.
Disc. first-pass effects and presystemic degradation where relevant.
Summ. tissue distribution studies: key organs, time-course, partitioning; include brain/placenta penetration where available.
Summ. plasma protein binding (% bound, concentration-dependence, species differences).
Summ. distribution in blood cells and tissue:blood or tissue:plasma ratios.
Summ. placental transfer and milk excretion data (pointer to 2.6.5.7 tables).
Desc. in vivo metabolite identification and quantitation (structures, relative abundance) across species.
Summ. in vitro metabolism (hepatocytes, microsomes; P450 phenotyping) identifying major enzymes and pathways.
Disc. presystemic/GI/hepatic first-pass metabolism and implications for exposure.
Comp. human vs animal metabolite profiles; flag human-unique or disproportionate metabolites.
Summ. routes and extent of elimination (urine, feces, bile, expired air) including mass-balance recoveries.
Prov. renal vs hepatic contribution estimates; note active secretion/reabsorption if evidenced.
Summ. excretion in milk and any neonatal exposure implications.

Summarize any nonclinical drug–drug interaction (DDI) studies conducted, including in vitro enzyme inhibition/induction and transporter assessments, as well as any in vivo DDI models. For macromolecules (e.g., peptides, proteins), such studies are generally not required unless specific criteria apply (e.g., >20% renal/hepatic clearance, hepatic-targeted mechanism, broad effects on protein expression, or potential PK modification via non-enzymatic pathways such as altered gastric transit).
Disc. mechanistic interpretations and translational relevance to human DDI risk.
Summ. PK in special animal models (renal/hepatic impairment, inflammation, age), linking to clinical special populations.

Integrate the ADME findings to identify key determinants of exposure and variability across species. Include concise PK parameter summary tables and, where relevant, exposure-bridging visualizations to support interpretation, ensuring consistent units and clear cross-referencing.

Discuss systemic exposure achieved in toxicology studies and note how these exposure ranges may inform initial clinical dosing. Detailed comparison to human MRHD will be addressed in the overall nonclinical/clinical integration once clinical PK and full toxicology data are available.
Address inconsistencies/uncertainties and method comparability limitations.
Incl. PK parameter summary tables and exposure-bridging plots; place within text or appended; ensure consistent units.
2–3 pages summarizing PK/ADME scope, species/strains, and formulation comparability.
Describe bioanalytical methods, LOD/LOQ, validation/stability, and interpretation impact.
Extent/rate; key PK parameters; bioavailability/bioequivalence evidence.
Tissue distribution, plasma protein binding/blood cell distribution, placental/lactational transfer.
Identify/quantify metabolites; pathways; first-pass; in vitro enzyme (e.g., CYP) work; induction/inhibition.
Routes and extent of elimination; include excretion in milk where available.
Summarize nonclinical PK interaction studies (in vitro/in vivo).
Summarize disease-state or special-population models if performed.
Integrate ADME findings; bridge animal exposure to human exposure at max intended dose.
Place key tables/figures inline or at section end; cross-reference clearly.
One-line per PK report: Absorption/Distribution/Metabolism/Excretion/Interactions; test system; route; facility; study/report number; CTD location; GLP footnote.

Columns: Species; Sex/n; Feeding; Vehicle/Formulation; Route; Dose (mg/kg); Matrix; Analyte; Assay; PK parameters (Cmax, Tmax, AUC, t1/2); Notes; Study No.; CTD Location; Human comparator, TK results with reference to toxicology report. Column format may be adapted to study design.
Same columns as single-dose; add steady-state parameters (Css, AUCtau, accumulation ratio). TK results with reference to toxicology report. Column format may be adapted to study design.
Columns: Tissue/Organ vs multiple sampling times (T1..Tn) with concentrations (unit) and optional t1/2; include dose, route, radionuclide, specific activity.
Columns: Tissue/Organ; Concentration; Tissue/Plasma ratio at timepoints; Last time-point conc; AUC; t1/2; analyte/assay; sampling times.
Columns: Species; Concentrations tested; % bound; test system/method; study no.; CTD location; notes.
Placental transfer: Dam vs Fetus concentrations/amount vs time; Excretion into milk: Milk, Plasma, Milk/Plasma ratio, Neonate exposure; include dose, day, n, analyte, assay.

Columns: Species; Sample (plasma/urine/bile/feces); Sampling time/period; % dose in sample; % parent and % metabolites (M1, M2…); Dose; Radionuclide; Specific activity; Study No.; CTD Location; add Human comparison if available.
Columns: Study system (matrix/species); Timepoints; Parent and metabolite concentrations; Enzymes implicated; Study No.; CTD Location; include human data if available.
Prov. metabolic map indicating species where each reaction occurs; annotate enzymes and relative contributions.
Columns: Study type; Method; Substrate/Probe; Concentration ranges; Effect size (% change); Kinetic parameters (Ki/EC50/Emax); Notes; Study No.; CTD Location.

Columns: Species; Sex/n; Feeding; Vehicle/Formulation; Route; Dose; Analyte; Assay; Excretion route (Urine, Feces, Bile, Total) by collection interval; Total recovery; Study No.; CTD Location; Human comparator column.
As per excretion table, focused on bile collection studies; include bile flow if available.
Columns: Interacting agent; System; Method; Doses/Concentrations; Effect on exposure (AUC, Cmax, CL); Mechanism; Study No.; CTD Location.
Custom tabulation for special PK studies (e.g., disease models); include key parameters and study identifiers.
Provide custom tabulations for special PK studies (e.g., QWBA, transporter phenotyping, hepatic uptake). Indicate system, method, and quantitative outputs.
Ensure every PK table cites Study/Report numbers, table/figure IDs, and cross-links to 4.x study reports; align naming with Appendix B conventions.
Prov. high-level overview (≤6 pages) of tox program scope vs intended clinical use; include GLP status summary.
Insert program table listing each tox study by type, duration, route, species, compound administered (parent/metabolite), without results.

Briefly state how study species and routes align with the intended clinical administration. Should generally have 2 species (rodent + non-rodent). If fewer than two species are used, provide the scientific rationale.

Summarize acute toxicity studies, including both dose-range-finding (non-GLP) and GLP pivotal studies, by species and route. Present the maximum tolerated dose, any observed lethality, and associated dose/exposure context.
Describe key clinical signs, onset and recovery patterns, and any sex-related differences across both dose-range-finding and GLP pivotal studies.
Indicate GLP status and any deviations impacting interpretation.
Summ. each study by species, route, and duration; include dose levels, toxicokinetics support, and exposure at NOAEL/toxic doses. Include dose range finding studies as well as GLP pivotal studies
Note target organ toxicities, dose-response, severity, reversibility, and recovery period outcomes.
Distinguish pivotal GLP studies from non-pivotal range-finding; reference ICH M3 alignment.
Disc. sex differences, age-related sensitivity, and strain-specific findings where applicable.
Summ. in vitro non-mammalian tests (e.g., Ames) with/without metabolic activation (S9); doses/concentrations and results.
Summ. in vitro mammalian assays (e.g., chromosome aberration, micronucleus) with/without S9; cytotoxicity and genotoxic outcomes.

Summarize in vivo mammalian genotoxicity studies (e.g., micronucleus, comet) only if conducted, typically in response to positive or equivocal in vitro findings or structural alerts. Where performed, include confirmation of systemic exposure (e.g., TK data), dosing and sampling schedules, and study outcomes.
Disc. weight of evidence and relevance to human risk; address positives/ambiguities and follow-ups.
Prov. rationale for species selection and high-dose selection per ICH S1 guidance.
Summ. long-term studies (by species), including survival, body weight, clinical observations, and neoplastic findings by tissue.
Summ. short-/medium-term studies and range-finding that inform dose selection if not captured under repeat-dose/PK.
Interpret tumor findings in context of genotoxicity and exposure; discuss human carcinogenic risk.
Summ. Fertility and Early Embryonic Development studies (mating indices, fertility indices, estrous, sperm parameters).
Summ. Embryo-Fetal Development studies (maternal toxicity, fetal viability, external/visceral/skeletal variations and malformations).
Summ. Prenatal and Postnatal Development studies (gestation, parturition, lactation, pup survival/growth/functional endpoints).
Summ. studies where offspring are dosed/evaluated (juvenile animals), if conducted, with age-dependent sensitivity considerations.
Incl. supportive TK where available; relate exposure margins to proposed clinical dosing in pregnancy/lactation/pediatrics.

Summarize local tolerance findings if local tolerance was evaluated or if the route of administration makes local effects clinically relevant. Present study species, route, duration, scoring methods, and key local reactions (e.g., irritation, inflammation, pain).
Where relevant, discuss whether observed local effects are attributable to the active ingredient, excipients, formulation properties, or delivery system.

Summarize any antigenicity or immunotoxicity evaluations performed, as appropriate for the molecule’s modality and mechanism of action. For biologics or immune-modulating agents, describe immune response assessments (e.g., ADA formation, cytokine profiling, immune organ histopathology) and discuss species/model relevance.
Summ. mechanistic studies clarifying tox findings not reported elsewhere (e.g., mode-of-action, target engagement in tox organs).
Summarize dependence or abuse liability assessments only if the pharmacology or clinical intent suggests CNS activity or reward pathway engagement.
Summ. metabolite toxicity studies (human disproportionate metabolites) and impurity toxicity studies where conducted.
Incl. any other relevant special toxicity studies and justify their conduct.
Integrate all tox domains; map target organs, severity, reversibility, and dose-response across species.
Prov. systemic exposure margins to human MRHD (AUC, Cmax) at NOAEL(s) and at toxic doses; highlight smallest margins.
Summ. uncertainties and limitations, and propose clinical monitoring/mitigations relevant to labeling.
Incl. summary tables/figures; place within text or appended; ensure consistency of units/statistics; cross-reference (Table X.X, Study/Report Number).
≤~6 pages; include table listing principal tox studies and scope vs intended clinical use; note GLP status.
Brief per species→route; summarize key findings; tables recommended.
Summarize by species→route→duration: target organs, severity, dose/exposure–response, NOAELs, reversibility; include supportive TK.
Summarize in vitro (non-mammalian & mammalian) and in vivo mammalian assays; include supportive TK.
Summarize long-term (per species), short/medium-term, and other studies; rationale/high-dose selection; include supportive TK.

Updated Module 2.6.Subsection: Reproductive and Developmental Toxicity (including range-finding studies and supportive toxicokinetics evaluations)
Updated Module 2.6.Content: Summarize fertility/early embryo, embryo‑fetal, pre/postnatal (incl. maternal) and juvenile studies; include range-finding & supportive TK.
Summarize by species→route→duration; methods brief with key findings.
Summarize antigenicity/immunotoxicity, mechanistic, dependence, metabolite/impurity studies, etc., with rationale.
Integrate across tox studies; provide risk characterization and exposure margins vs human at max intended dose.
Place key tables/figures inline or at section end; cross-reference clearly.
Columns: Study Type; Species/Strain; Route; Duration; Dose levels (mg/kg; underline highest NOAEL); GLP; Testing Facility; Study/Report No.; CTD Location.
Columns: Study Type; Test System; Route; Doses; GLP; Study No.; CTD Location (covering TK studies supporting tox).
Prov. 1–3 pages of tables/figures summarizing steady-state TK across species (AUC, Cmax, Css), facilitating species-human comparisons.

Columns: Batch No.; Purity (%); Specified Impurities; Study/Report No.; Study Type; Proposed Clinical Specification; Identify which GLP tox studies used each batch. Note that research-grade batches may not have full release specifications; ensure GLP study batches are clearly distinguished.
Columns: Species/Strain; Method/Route (Vehicle/Formulation); Doses (mg/kg); Sex/n; Observed Max Non-lethal Dose; Approximate Lethal Dose; Noteworthy Findings; Study No.
Columns: Species/Strain; Route; Duration; Doses; Sex/n; NOAEL; Noteworthy Findings; Study No.; CTD Location.

One table per pivotal study including: doses; animals per sex; TK (AUC/Cmax/Css); deaths; BW/food/water; clinical obs; ophthalmo; ECG; hematology; chemistry; urinalysis; organ weights; gross pathology; histopathology; postdose evaluations; stats.

One table per assay: strains/cell lines; activation (+/− S9); doses; cytotoxicity; genotoxic outcomes; precipitation; stats; Study No.; CTD Location. Not generally required for oncology agents or most biologics

One table per assay: species/strain; treatment schedule; sampling time; route; vehicle; cells/tissue; n analyzed; toxicity/cytotoxicity; genotoxic outcomes; evidence of exposure (TK); stats; Study No.; CTD Location. Required only if in vitro genotoxicity results are positive or equivocal; otherwise optional.
One per study: species/strain; duration; route; vehicle; high-dose rationale; survival; BW; clinical obs; neoplastic lesions by tissue; noteworthy gross/histo; TK; statistics. Not needed for IND
Separate tables: Fertility/EED; EFD; PPND; Juvenile; include design factors, maternal/paternal toxicity, fetal/offspring endpoints, malformations/variations; TK where available. Not needed for IND

Columns: Species; Route; Duration; Scoring system; Local findings; Reversibility; Study No.; CTD Location. May be included within repeat-dose toxicity tables when injection-site reactions are captured there.

Columns tailored to study type: Antigenicity; Immunotoxicity; Mechanistic; Dependence; Metabolites; Impurities; include endpoints and key results. For biologics, antigenicity is required but is often already captured in repeat-dose tox tables. Include additional immunotoxicity or mechanistic immune studies only when scientifically justified (e.g., immune-modulating products such as mRNA vaccines). If immune mechanism data are central to the MOA, they may be presented in Pharmacology rather than Toxicology.
Ensure all tables include Study/Report numbers and CTD locations; GLP compliance status; keep consistent table numbering per CTD.

Within each subsection: present in vitro before in vivo; order by species → route → duration. Species order: mouse → rat → hamster → other rodent → rabbit → dog → NHP → other mammals → non-mammals. Route order: intended clinical route first, then oral, IV, IM, IP, SC, inhalation, topical, other. (as general guidelines, but variation may exist)

Use SI units; consisent on number of decimal places/significant figures; define abbreviations on first use; state assay validation status; specify whether values are mean±SD/SEM, geometric means, medians; identify censored or BQL handling.
